claims.claim: Andy Lee says the narrator's voice constructs the world of a novel by revealing some truths and concealing others.
claims.quote: revealing some truths and concealing others

claims.claim: Andy Lee says Wolfe never shows the reader the monster of Peace directly.
claims.quote: Wolfe never shows you the monster directly.

claims.claim: Andy Lee likens Wolfe's method in Peace to hiding the answers in plain sight.
claims.quote: the hiding of answers in plain sight

claims.claim: Andy Lee says Peace could be the story of a conventional life except that its gaps are troubling.
claims.quote: It could be the story of a conventional life, but the gaps

claims.claim: Andy Lee says the narrator of Peace is searching in his memories but also trying to conceal a great deal more.
claims.quote: he’s also trying to conceal a whole lot more

claims.claim: Andy Lee reads a Peace bookseller's line about a forged volume — that it is nevertheless catalogued — as capturing how a record confers existence on what it lists.
claims.quote: but nevertheless it is catalogued, there it is on the page

claims.claim: Andy Lee reports that Wolfe's own comments on Peace suggest he worried he had concealed too well for readers to follow.
claims.source: Andy Lee, Lit & Chess (Substack), 12 July 2026, relaying unspecified comments by Gene Wolfe
claims.quote: he was concerned that he’d done too good of a job
